title: Territory access gate and customer permitlist handshake
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Purpose: implement a deterministic ‘territory access gate’ that evaluates customer-scoped permitlists/denylist rules, contract-level residency constraints, and tier routing policies to decide region selection and model-variant fallbacks. This ticket implements the runtime decision handshake (fast-path) plus audit envelope emitted for each decision. The goal is a single-pass policy evaluator with clear precedence, deterministic fallbacks, and hooks for operator overrides.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Requests with customer metadata containing region-scoped residency:true must never egress to non-EU regions; attempts should return a routed endpoint in EU or a documented 409-like signal if capacity unavailable.
2) Customer permitlist (explicit allow of non-EU routing) is honored only when contract_flag.allow_crossborder == true; otherwise ignore permitlist entries that widen egress.
3) Tier routing (premium vs standard) is used as a tie-breaker when multiple regional endpoints satisfy residency constraints; premium tiers are preferred if latency delta < configured threshold.

4) When preferred model variant is unavailable, fallback follows model-variant precedence table (contract pinned > tenant preferred > global default) and never selects a lower-residency endpoint than allowed by residency constraints.

5) Every decision emits a compact audit envelope: policy_version, evaluated_rules, chosen_endpoint, fallback_reason, latency_estimate, trace_id. Telemetry must appear in Console per-route model table within 2 minutes of rollout.
6) Integration tests simulate saturation -> verify automatic canary fallback to allowed variant and that metric-based alarms fire (SLO: <1% incorrect routing decisions in test harness).
tasks: Design policy precedence matrix and DSL fingerprints (collab with PM & Compliance)
Implement fast-path evaluator in routing service (C++) with O(1) cost for most requests
Add audit envelope builder and wire to observability pipeline (logs + metric tags)
Expose per-customer override token that ops can use to temporarily open a route (with expiry)
Create integration test harness that replays production trace sample and asserts no residency leaks
Update Console to display decision reason and permitlist source in call details
design_decisions: Precedence order: contract-level constraints > customer permit/deny lists > region-default policy > runtime emergency override
Permitlist entries that widen egress require an explicit contract flag; otherwise permitlist is treated as advisory only
Fast-path is purely in-memory rule evaluation using precompiled rule fingerprints; async refresh from central policy store every 30s
Fallback selection prefers same-region model variants first, then same-continent, then cross-continent only if allowed by contract and customer permitlist
Use existing routing circuit breaker to prevent cascading cross-border failover during region outage (configurable window and cooldown)
risks: Mis-evaluated precedence could unintentionally route EU-restricted traffic out of region — high regulatory risk
Performance regression if policy evaluation falls back to datastore lookups; mitigate via in-memory cache and warmup
Operational complexity for per-customer overrides may be abused — require audit trail and short TTLs
Telemetry lag could delay detection of incorrect routing; ensure sampling + sinks are prioritized for compliance events
rollout_plan: Phase A (internal): run evaluator in read-only shadow mode for 48h against 10% of traffic. Verify audit envelopes and false-positive rate <0.1%
Phase B (canary): enable enforcement for 5% of accounts (non-high-risk) with ops guardrails and fast rollback script
Phase C (gradual): ramp enforcement 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 weeks after sign-off from Security & Legal
Rollback: immediate revert to previous routing binary + invalidate local policy cache; postmortem required for any incorrect routing event
Post-rollout: 30d audit with sampled requests verified against contract records and retention of envelopes for 90 days
